name: probes
description: Benign, non-destructive checks: single safe requests that flag a real exposure only when it is actually present.
author: Plonix

tactics.title: Exposed .git/config
tactics.description: The version-control directory is reachable over HTTP, which can leak source code and history.
tactics.remediation: Block access to the .git directory at the web server or move the working tree out of the web root.

tactics.title: Exposed .env file
tactics.description: An environment file is reachable over HTTP and may contain secrets.
tactics.remediation: Serve application files only; deny access to dotfiles and move secrets out of the web root.

tactics.title: Apache server-status exposed
tactics.description: The server-status page is reachable and discloses request and client information.
tactics.remediation: Restrict mod_status to localhost or trusted networks.

tactics.title: Parameter reflected in response
tactics.description: A request parameter is echoed back in the response body. Reflection is not itself a vulnerability, but it is where output-encoding issues show up, so the endpoint is worth reviewing. The probe value is a harmless marker.
tactics.remediation: Contextually encode any user input that is written into a response.

tactics.title: GraphQL schema is enumerable
tactics.description: The GraphQL endpoint answers an introspection query, so its full schema — every type, field and argument — can be enumerated. That is useful to an attacker mapping the API. The probe sends a standard, read-only introspection query and only flags the endpoint when a schema comes back.
tactics.remediation: Disable introspection in production, or allow it only for authorized roles.

tactics.title: Exposed .git/HEAD
tactics.description: The Git HEAD file is reachable over HTTP, a strong sign the whole .git directory is served and source history can be reconstructed.
tactics.remediation: Deny access to the .git directory at the web server, or move the working tree out of the web root.

tactics.title: OpenAPI description exposed
tactics.description: A machine-readable OpenAPI (Swagger) description is served, listing every route, parameter and schema. It is often meant for internal use and hands an attacker a full API map.
tactics.remediation: Serve the API description only to authenticated internal users, or not in production.

tactics.title: Swagger description exposed
tactics.description: A Swagger API description is served at a common path, listing routes and schemas that are often meant to stay internal.
tactics.remediation: Serve the API description only to authenticated internal users, or not in production.

tactics.title: Directory listing enabled
tactics.description: The web root returns an automatic directory index, which can expose files that were never meant to be linked.
tactics.remediation: Turn off automatic directory indexing at the web server.

tactics.title: phpinfo() page exposed
tactics.description: A phpinfo() page is reachable and discloses the PHP version, loaded modules, environment variables and server paths.
tactics.remediation: Remove phpinfo() pages from anything reachable in production.

tactics.title: WordPress users enumerable
tactics.description: The WordPress REST API lists user accounts, including their login slugs, which is useful for targeting password attacks.
tactics.remediation: Restrict or disable the users REST endpoint, or require authentication for it.

tactics.title: WordPress XML-RPC enabled
tactics.description: The XML-RPC interface is enabled. It accepts POST requests and has historically been abused for brute-force amplification and server-side request relaying.
tactics.remediation: Disable XML-RPC if it is not needed, or block access to xmlrpc.php.
